schedule.summary: Hours you are away, busy, or not shown at all, repeated every week.
schedule.notSaved: That schedule could not be saved
schedule.deleteDescription: {schedule}. This cannot be undone - to keep it for later, switch it off instead.

zone.assumed: These run on the clock of whichever machine Polaris is on. Pick a timezone in Preferences to be sure they run on yours.
zone.pinned: Times are read on your own clock ({zone}).
zone.browser: Times are read on this browser's clock ({zone}). Pick a timezone in Preferences to keep them on one.

page.title: Privacy
page.intro: Who can find you, who sees your details, and who sees what you are doing. Everything here can be answered with everybody, nobody, or a set of people you name.

adminNote: Who counts as a friend is on your <link>friends page</link>. Whoever administers this Polaris can see all of it whatever you choose here. They can read the database, so a setting that claimed otherwise would not be true.

discoverable.label: Whether people can find you
discoverable.note: Who finds your account when they look for somebody. Anybody who cannot has to know your exact username to ask to be added, and is never told whether it exists.

lastSeen.label: When you were last here
lastSeen.note: Whether other people can see that you are here now, or when you last were.

activity.label: What you are playing or listening to
activity.note: The game or song shown beside your name. Only ever shown to people who can also see that you are here, and never while you appear offline.

readReceipts.label: That you have read a message
readReceipts.note: The ticks under a message in a direct conversation. Turning this down also stops you seeing anybody else's, and "only" is how you leave them on for one person.

avatar.label: Your photo
avatar.note: Who sees your photo. Anybody who cannot gets your initials instead.

photoFullSize.label: Opening your photo
photoFullSize.note: Who can open your photo and look at it full size. Anybody who cannot still sees it beside your name - this is a rule about the press, not a second copy of the picture.

fullName.label: Your full name
fullName.note: Who sees the name on your account rather than the name you show. Anybody who cannot sees your display name, which is what every screen draws anyway.

email.label: Your email address
email.note: Who sees the address you sign in with. Anybody who cannot sees your name and username, which is enough to write to you here.

phone.label: Your phone number
phone.note: The number kept for sign-in codes. Nobody is shown it unless you say so.

companies.label: Where you work
companies.note: The company on your profile, and the organizations here you have chosen to show. Which organizations those are is picked one at a time on your profile; this decides who sees the ones you picked.

followers.label: The names behind your follower counts
followers.note: Who can open the two lists of names on your profile. The counts are always shown - how many follow you is a fact about you, and it is on your page the way the day you joined is - so this is about the several other people in the lists, who never chose to be on your page. Your administrator sets what a new account starts on; this is yours.

friendRequests.label: Who can ask to be your friend
friendRequests.note: Who may ask. Anybody turned down here is not told they were - the button is simply not offered - and nobody is ever stopped from following you, which asks nothing of you. Set to nobody, only the requests already waiting can still be answered.

fileTransfers.label: Who can send you files
fileTransfers.note: Who may offer you a file or a folder. Nothing ever lands without you accepting it, so this is about who may ask - anybody who cannot is simply not offered the button. People you share an organization with count as friends here; set to nobody, nobody can, including them.

calls.label: Who can call you
calls.note: Who may ring you. A call takes over the screen of whatever you were doing and makes a noise in the room you are in, which is why this starts at your friends rather than at everybody. Joining a voice channel is not this: that is a room somebody walked into, and who may be in it is the room's own question. Anybody who cannot call you is simply not offered the button.

forwarding.label: Passing your messages on
forwarding.note: Who may forward something you wrote into another conversation. Anybody who cannot is not offered it, and they can still copy the text - this is a rule about the button, not a lock on your words.

who.emptyList: That list is empty, so this names nobody.
who.nobody: Nobody named yet, so this does nothing.

lists.title: Lists
lists.empty: A list is a set of people you can point more than one setting at - the people you hide your number from, the ones who see when you were last here. Settings can also name people on their own row without one.
lists.deleteDescription: The people on it are not told, and nothing else changes.
lists.dialogDescription: Name it for what it is for. Nobody on it is ever told they are.
lists.name: Name

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.description: They cannot message, call or mention you, and what they write where you both are is folded away. They are not told.
blocked.empty: Nobody. You can block somebody from the menu on their name.

errors.notSaved: Those settings could not be saved

errors.cannotUnblock: That is not somebody this can unblock

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: What you are playing or listening to, shown beside your name. Only people who can see that you are here see it, and nobody sees it while you appear offline.
activity.shareHint: Off hides all of it, from everybody.

spotify.linked: The song your linked Spotify is playing, while you are here. People who see it can listen along.
spotify.unlinked: Link your Spotify under <link>Connected accounts</link> and the song you are playing shows here.
spotify.unavailable: Not available yet: whoever runs this Polaris has not connected Spotify to it.

games.label: Games on your computer
games.hint: Seen by the Polaris desktop app on Windows, macOS and Linux. A browser cannot see what else is running, so this only works while the desktop app is open.

minecraft.label: Minecraft servers here
minecraft.hint: When you play on one of this Polaris's Minecraft servers as a player linked to your account.
